where: help.go: help, what a key does

id: A command is a prompt saved in a Markdown file that you start by typing /name. Claude Code now treats commands like skills; the difference is that a skill can also be chosen by Claude itself.

A hook is a shell command that Claude Code (not Claude) runs on an event: before or after a tool, when you send a message, when a session ends. Use one for what must always happen, such as formatting.
A plugin is a package of skills, subagents, commands, hooks and MCP servers that you install and switch on together from a marketplace.

A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md: instructions and files Claude loads only when a task needs them. Only its name and description are always in context. Use one for a way of doing something you repeat.
A subagent is a separate Claude with its own context, tools and model. The main conversation hands it a task and gets back a summary, so long searches and reviews do not fill your context.
a system notification when a Claude Code session finishes and waits for you
An MCP server gives Claude tools to reach another system: GitHub, a database, a browser. The definitions of its tools take context in every session where it is on.
at least one tab must stay visible
at this pace it runs out before the reset
auto follows your terminal background; mono uses no colour
